newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. revised Q1 GDP up 5.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. revised Q1 GDP up 5.8 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Commerce Department reported its second estimate for first quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth at 5.8 percent compared to a previosuly released 5.6 percent expansion rate.
U.S. economists in a Reuters survey had expected first quarter GDP to be revised up to 6.0 percent.
JOSHUA FEINMAN, VICE PRESIDENT AND GLOBAL MARKETS ECONOMIST, BANKERS TRUST: "The revision was very much as expected.

"So what we knew before, we still know. We're looking for real GDP to grow between 1.5 percent and 2.0 percent in the second quarter. As far as Fed policy is concerned, the Fed is paying close attention to demand volatility. Retail sales were weak in April. We'll see what May and June brings," Bhagavatula added.

DAN SETO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, THE NIKKO SECURITIES CO INTERNATIONAL INC: "The difference in the picture is you have a lot more inventory building and that may be viewed by some, going forward, as providing less work in the pipeline for manufacturers. Some may use that to argue for slower growth in the second quarter."

FRED STURM, ECONOMIST, FUJI SECURITIES INC: "The difference is a hair spread. It's essentially not different from the original number. It's still plenty strong; this was a minor adjustment to what is fundamentally a big number. Anyone who puts on a trade (on the revision) is trading on noise in the data."

GARY THAYER, SENIOR ECONOMIST, A.G. EDWARDS & SONS INC: "The report still shows the economy is very strong in the first quarter, but not necessarily that much stronger than what the government reported earlier.
"We still think that even though final sales were revised downward, that really doesn't change the complexion of the first quarter growth rate.

"We think recent economic reports suggest that the economy will growth slower here in the second quarter than what we saw in the first quarter ... We're looking for growth to be around 2.0 to 2.5 percent in the second quarter."

MICHAEL NIEMIRA, ECONOMIST, BANK OF TOKYO-MITSUBISHI LTD: "It was not much of a revision and, in essence, a yawner ... the after-tax profits number did show a first quarter rise of 4.5 percent, but that was actually a little less than I expected. (The upward revision in inventories) was the story everybody was expecting and that was actually less than I was looking for. Basically the story line is there, it doesn't change anything looking forward ... all the changes seem to be small.
"There was one exception in corporate profits. There were gains but they rose less than S&P profit measures."
